# Abstract {.unnumbered}

Electric Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) technology requires intelligent scheduling to balance grid needs with user convenience. This paper presents a data-driven V2G scheduler that determines WHEN, WHY, and WHO for optimal discharge timing. We analyzed 72,856 real charging sessions from 2,337 EV users and integrated this with grid pricing data from the California Independent System Operator (CAISO). Our analysis reveals that only 5.1% of sessions are suitable for V2G, occuring primarily during 5-8 PM when both grid demand and electricity prices peak. The scheduler employs a scoring system combining time windows (40 points), user history (30 points), and battery state (20 points) to make V2G decisions. Testing demonstrates potential to increase V2G participation from 5.1% to 12% through targeted user engagement, yielding \$1.31/user/year revenue in an optimistic scenario. Integration with the EVerest charging simulator demonstrates real-time decision making capabilities, prioritizing user needs while maximizing grid support during peak hours.
